challenges.name: secrets-in-logs-quiz
challenges.title: Where else does the secret show up?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the config-loader incident: a CI step that encodes a masked secret, and a pull request that removed the config dump but kept the error message.

questions.question:
A step in .github/workflows/smoke.yml:

- name: Smoke test the sandbox
  env:
    SANDBOX_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SANDBOX_API_KEY }}
  run: |
    echo "key=$SANDBOX_API_KEY"
    echo "auth=$(printf 'codedev:%s' "$SANDBOX_API_KEY" | base64 -w0)"

Job log:
key=***
auth=Y29kZWRldjpzYnhfRkFLRV83ZjNhOWMyZTViOGQxMDQ2

Statement: "The runner masked the key on the first line, so the second line does not expose it either."
questions.explanation: False. GitHub Actions masks the exact string of each registered secret wherever it appears in the log. The second line is a different string: base64 of "codedev:" plus the key, and anyone can decode it with base64 -d to get the key back. The same gap applies to any transformation - URL-encoding, JSON escaping, a substring, a value split across two lines - and to values the runner never knew were secret, such as a key read from a file during the job. The fix is not to print derived values at all (or to register them with ::add-mask:: before use) and to rotate the key, because this log has already been stored. The misconception is that masking understands the secret; it is a find-and-replace on one exact string.

True. The thrown error carries the whole URL, including the user:password part, in its message, and the top-level handler prints the error (message and stack) with console.error, which goes to the same deploy log. Error messages also travel further than log lines: error trackers, crash reports and CI annotations copy them. The fix is to report the variable by name only ("invalid DATABASE_URL"), never its value, and to test the thrown message as well as the log output. The misconception is that secrets leak only through log statements; any string that reaches stdout or stderr, including an exception, is a log.

challenges.name: config-loader-secret-logs
challenges.title: Fix it: a config loader that prints secrets
challenges.description:
src/config.ts is the first code that runs in the CodeDev API server, in next build on CI and in every preview deploy. CI build #1187 failed with "LOG_LEVEL invalid: verbose", and the line just above that error in the public build log printed the whole configuration as JSON, SANDBOX_API_KEY included. A preview deploy crashed with "DATABASE_URL invalid: postgres:/codedev_app:<password>@..." in a log the whole team can read. Even a successful start shows DATABASE_URL and SANDBOX_API_KEY in clear text.

Fix loadConfig(env, log) so that no secret value (a SCHEMA entry with secret: true) is ever logged or put in an error message. A variable is missing when it is unset or empty; defaults apply to optional ones. If any required variable is missing or any present value fails its check, log nothing and throw one Error with the message "Invalid configuration: missing A, B; invalid C" - names only, in SCHEMA order, leaving out the "missing ..." or "invalid ..." part when it is empty. Otherwise log exactly one line, "config ok: " followed by NAME=value for every SCHEMA entry in SCHEMA order, separated by single spaces: a non-secret shows its value, an optional variable that is not set shows NAME=(unset), and a secret shows "***" plus its last 4 characters when the value has 20 or more characters, or only "***" when it is shorter.

The runner reads { env }, prints every logged line as "log: <line>", then "ok" or "error: <message>", then "leaked: <NAME>" for each secret whose full value appears anywhere in that output. Do not change the schema or the test runner. Every secret in the tests is fake.
hints: Count the places where a string leaves loadConfig: every call to log and every thrown Error. For each one, ask which variables can end up inside it, and whether the code decides "is this a secret?" from the schema or from something else.

Look at the line right after the config object is built, at the two throw statements inside the validation loop (what do they include, and how many problems can they report?), and at how the summary decides which values to mask and how mask treats a short value.

A similar case on other input: a schema with SMTP_HOST (not secret), SMTP_PASSWORD (secret, required) and WEBHOOK_URL (secret, must start with https://). With SMTP_PASSWORD unset and WEBHOOK_URL = "http://hooks.test/abc", the loader logs nothing and throws "Invalid configuration: missing SMTP_PASSWORD; invalid WEBHOOK_URL". With valid values, a 9-character password shows as "***" and a 30-character webhook URL as "***" plus its last 4 characters.

tests.name: A valid production config logs one summary with secrets masked
tests.expected:
log: config ok: NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080 LOG_LEVEL=info PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://app.codedev.test DATABASE_URL=***edev REDIS_URL=***6380 JWT_SECRET=***0000 SANDBOX_API_KEY=***1046
ok

tests.name: The incident: CI build with LOG_LEVEL=verbose fails by name, logs nothing
Missing and invalid together; the bad DATABASE_URL is not echoed
tests.expected: error: Invalid configuration: missing JWT_SECRET; invalid DATABASE_URL

tests.name: Empty environment: every required name, in schema order
tests.expected: error: Invalid configuration: missing NODE_ENV, PUBLIC_APP_URL, DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, SANDBOX_API_KEY

tests.name: Defaults, empty values, an unset optional secret, 19- and 20-character secrets
tests.expected:
log: config ok: NODE_ENV=development PORT=3000 LOG_LEVEL=info PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://localhost.codedev.test DATABASE_URL=*** REDIS_URL=(unset) JWT_SECRET=***0000 SANDBOX_API_KEY=***aaaa
ok

tests.name: Short REDIS_URL secret shows only *** (no last 4 characters)
tests.expected:
log: config ok: NODE_ENV=production PORT=8080 LOG_LEVEL=info PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://app.codedev.test DATABASE_URL=***edev REDIS_URL=*** JWT_SECRET=***0000 SANDBOX_API_KEY=***1046
ok

tests.name: Invalid input: wrong values everywhere, one missing secret
tests.expected: error: Invalid configuration: missing DATABASE_URL; invalid NODE_ENV, PORT, LOG_LEVEL, PUBLIC_APP_URL, REDIS_URL, JWT_SECRET, SANDBOX_API_KEY

tests.name: Large CI environment: 1400 unrelated variables and other tokens are ignored
tests.expected:
log: config ok: NODE_ENV=production PORT=443 LOG_LEVEL=info PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://app.codedev.test DATABASE_URL=***edev REDIS_URL=***6380 JWT_SECRET=***0000 SANDBOX_API_KEY=***1046
ok
